title: Jumping and Splashing
checkpoint: Year 1 Summer 2, week 2 — School readiness — Phase 6: new sounds -ing, -ed
note_for_grown_ups: A Phase 6 book for the endings '-ing' and '-ed'. Listen out for the three different ways '-ed' can sound: jumped (/t/), splashed (/t/), landed (/id/). Don't teach the rule — just enjoy noticing it.

pages.text: Ned was jumping. He jumped off the log, and then he jumped off the rock.
pages.illustration: Ned mid-air over the pond in a tucked jump, legs pulled in, sheer joy on his face. Below him the log and the rock he has already used. Motion arcs drawn faintly. Bright and splashy.

pages.text: Pip was looking on. He did not like to get wet, so he stayed up on the fence.
pages.illustration: Pip on a fence post above the pond, entirely dry, wings folded, radiating disapproval. Ned's splash reaching almost but not quite up to him.

pages.text: Fig was resting. Resting is what Fig is best at.
pages.illustration: Fig the green striped caterpillar stretched full length along a warm cabbage leaf in the sun, all his little legs relaxed, eyes shut. Extremely comfortable. Big flat leaf shapes.

pages.text: Ned splashed. He splashed Pip, and Pip squawked.
pages.illustration: The moment of impact: a wall of water arriving at the fence post, Pip erupting in a flap of shocked feathers and one indignant open beak. Big diagonal splash shape.

pages.text: Pip was flapping and shouting and dripping all at the same time.
pages.illustration: Pip hopping about on the fence rail, wings out, water running off his tail feathers, absolutely furious. Ned in the pond below with an innocent expression. Peak comedy.

pages.text: Then Fig rolled off his leaf and landed in the pond, and he did not jump at all that day.
pages.illustration: Fig tumbling sideways off the cabbage leaf, all legs waving, with a small startled expression. A neat little splash below. Everybody else has stopped to look.

pages.text: They pulled him out. He was soaked, and he was smiling.
pages.illustration: Fig lying on the bank in a wet green heap, thoroughly bedraggled, grinning. Ned and Pip either side of him, both dripping too, all three friends again. Warm evening light.

pages.text: After that, they all jumped. Pip did too. Pip most of all.
pages.illustration: Final full-page spread: all three in mid-air over the pond at once, Pip highest of all with his wings spread wide and his eyes shut in delight. Big joyful splash forming below.
